newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MKT RATES STABLE IN LIQUID TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MKT RATES STABLE IN LIQUID TRADE.

text.p: Short term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market held stable at their overnight levels on Tuesday but dealers expected them to shed a few points on the back of liquidity during the week.
"The market is fairly liquid at the moment. In fact the whole of this week we're expecting quite a number of treasury bill maturities and rates could go down," one dealer said.
Discount houses were purchasing 91-day treasury bills from the central Reserve Bank at 19 percent and re-selling them in the market at 18.85 percent.

Negotiable certificates of deposit with maturity of 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at a steady 20.50 percent and sold at 19 percent and bankers acceptances were also quoted unchanged at 19.50 (buying) and 18.85 percent (selling) across the board.
Call money was at Monday's 19 percent with Reserve Bank figures indicating a market surplus of Z$442 million before settlement, up from the previous Z$52.3 million.
